title: Product boundary
requirement: EQM verifies product conformance; it does not implement accounts, tasks, business media storage, synchronization, UI frameworks, or deployment infrastructure.

title: Runtime roles
requirement: Treat the Rust product CLI, KMP desktop control tower, KMP mobile edge, and relevant providers as distinct participants; the EQM CLI is a separate developer tool.

title: Deployment scope
requirement: Start with developer tooling and CI plus native test/runtime adapters; embedded mobile evaluation, a desktop daemon, and native bindings are optional, not automatic v1 deliverables.

title: Shared engine
requirement: A single normative pure Rust evaluator serves CLI, matrices, MCP, release checks, and attestations through a thin shared application layer.

title: Effect separation
requirement: Acquisition may perform explicitly authorized I/O and execution; evaluation consumes frozen inputs without ambient filesystem, network, environment, or clock discovery.

title: Layering
requirement: Preserve domain, manifest, engine, protocol, runner, and MCP boundaries; avoid dependency cycles, duplicate semantics, gratuitous microcrates, or microservices.

title: Target model
requirement: Separate product role, independently shipped target/build output, source ownership, shared dependencies, and scenario participant identity.

title: Participation
requirement: Declare approved requirement/target/profile participation; intentional role differences are not waivers; unknown applicability remains visible.

title: Comparability
requirement: Shared comparison context must be separate from exact per-participant build/artifact/configuration identity; support approved mixed-version combinations.

title: Claim limits
requirement: Conformance is scoped to authored contracts and evidence; equivalence is contract-relative, with explicit relational checks where actual cross-target agreement is required.

title: Completeness
requirement: Every required coordinate is evaluated, explicitly non-applicable, or unresolved; completeness is validated and cannot be asserted by an untrusted boolean.

title: Empty scope
requirement: Empty required release scope cannot authorize by vacuous truth; singleton comparisons are not a meaningful cross-target equivalence claim.

title: All scopes
requirement: Evaluate target, shared-provider, and end-to-end obligations, including role-specific repeated participants and dependency effects.

title: Normative semantics
requirement: Document and test applicability, coverage, freshness, trust, attempts, counts, status precedence, and per-facet policy composition independently of implementation.

title: No false success
requirement: Unknown, missing, stale, unstable, failed, skipped, filtered, quarantined, insufficiently trusted, and waived states are not satisfied evidence.

title: Count integrity
requirement: Count explicit distinct selected observations/cases rather than files or retries; bind expected selection inventory to execution.

title: Campaign history
requirement: Preserve immutable attempts within an authorized campaign; select campaigns by explicit policy, retain history, prohibit cherry-picking and permanent poisoning by unrelated old campaigns.

title: Three identities
requirement: Distinguish raw bytes, normalized semantic evidence, and execution/attempt identity; identical imports are idempotent and conflicting immutable attempts are visible.

title: Precise digests
requirement: Use domain-separated versioned semantic projections and executable/toolchain/source provenance; do not hash only display coordinates or reuse workspace digest for unrelated fields.

title: Acyclic records
requirement: Candidate subject precedes plan, evidence, frozen inputs, decision, statement, authorization, and deployment receipt; prevent digest self-reference.

title: Canonical protocol
requirement: Specify canonical JSON, duplicates, numeric bounds, Unicode preservation, set/sequence ordering, null/absence, and time precision; preserve original signed bytes.

title: Frozen provenance
requirement: Trusted runs use immutable approved inputs; local dirty state is explicit; evaluation cannot mix generations of live reads.

title: Protected authority
requirement: Protected release authority covers policy, contracts, participation, evidence mappings, selections, waivers, trust configuration, and the evaluator itself; candidates cannot grade themselves.

title: Trust acceptance
requirement: Cryptographic validity, identity/issuer, authorization, producer/build, exact subject, and temporal/revocation constraints are independently checked; claims cannot raise trust.

title: Verification integration
requirement: Use reviewed cryptography and a real verifier integration; Sigstore bundles are the approved default CI direction, with provider-neutral internal boundaries and explicit configuration.

title: Receipt integrity
requirement: Persist exact verification context; imported verified flags, public constructors, or test-only synthetic trust cannot manufacture production authority.

title: Release separation
requirement: Evaluation, signing, release authorization, and deployment are distinct; signed failures remain failures and unknown never authorizes.

title: Exposure and timing
requirement: Compare actual runtime facts to expectations; distinguish pre-release readiness from post-deployment conformance; observations cannot be required before they can exist.

title: Waivers
requirement: Only approved scoped time-bounded exceptions contribute to conditional conclusions; no fabricated evidence, implicit approvals, automatic renewal, or blanket waiver inclusion.

title: Concrete execution plan
requirement: Dry-run resolves and reports exact executable, argv, cwd, selector, environment references, limits, capabilities, and outputs without executing; bind execution to approval.

title: Worker isolation
requirement: Workers and executable discovery adapters cannot write authority, evaluator, durable evidence store, or signing credentials; choose isolation matching the host threat model.

title: Whole lifecycle bounds
requirement: Timeout, cancellation, overflow, descendant cleanup, output drainage, and errors are supervised for the entire invocation, with explicit supported-host guarantees.

title: Bounded filesystem
requirement: Use confined handle-based access, bounded preallocation/read limits, post-execution result checks, and race-aware writes; claimed artifact roles are not observations.

title: Secrets and environment
requirement: No implicit network or inherited environment; resolve authorized secret references, redact retained output, and never render secrets or assume redaction prevents exfiltration.

title: Persistence
requirement: Immutable content-addressed objects plus a transactional local index; publish objects durably before committing references and recover orphans without phantom completed records.

title: SQLite operations
requirement: Use an audited SQLite build with the WAL-reset fix, local-host WAL, short transactions, bounded writer contention, explicit checkpoint ownership, and tested durability.

title: Retention and privacy
requirement: Define retention classes, reader/run leases, GC reachability, archived release protection, and sensitive attachment handling; immutability does not require infinite retention.

title: Replay versus current acceptance
requirement: Historical decisions remain replayable; current acceptance reevaluates freshness, authority, revocation, and deployment conditions without rewriting history.

title: Safe caching
requirement: Stage caches with complete identities, trust/evaluator versions, validity boundaries, and event invalidation; no stale pass reuse.

title: Affected analysis
requirement: Reverse dependencies include shared sources, contract/profile/runner/adapter/trust changes; unknown or deleted paths widen impact conservatively; wire verify --affected.

title: Batching and concurrency
requirement: Batch test invocations by runner/target/device/selection; bounded queues, device exclusivity, deterministic aggregation, and explicit cancellation precede concurrency optimization.

title: Global resource limits
requirement: Bound parsing depth/bytes, graph expansion, profile combinations, candidate evidence, attachment sizes, queues, and requests; limits never silently remove obligations.

title: Reference equivalence
requirement: Compare optimized results to a simple reference path and realistic end-to-end benchmarks; declared budgets are not measured results.

title: Coherent interfaces
requirement: CLI check/matrix/context/MCP/report/attestation views derive from the same snapshot and explanation records; filters do not recompute scope or completeness.

title: Protocol errors
requirement: Stable machine errors with context and source locations across CLI/MCP/optional SDK; errors under JSON output remain machine-readable where parsing permits.

title: Safe reports
requirement: Expose snapshot identity, scope, freshness, trust, reasons, waivers, and truncation; snapshot-bound pagination/incremental updates must not overstate assurance.

title: MCP permissions
requirement: Read-only by default, private stdio or restricted IPC, bounded requests, untrusted text labeling, and separate explicit authorization for any mutating/executing capability.

title: Cross-runtime fixtures
requirement: Verify mobile offline capture/edit/restart/sync, desktop correct revision, and CLI inspect/export with no duplicates or cross-account disclosure; include failure and compatibility cases.

title: Optional SDK safety
requirement: When explicitly activated, choose one proven bridge; define ownership, handles, cancellation, threading, numeric mappings, version negotiation, and target packaging; JNA Kotlin is not Kotlin/Native.

title: Code conventions
requirement: Typed contextual errors/newtypes, private validation boundaries, immutable inputs, narrow traits, explicit lifecycle state, no ambient globals, and no production panic/synthetic trust shortcuts.

title: Unsafe boundaries
requirement: Keep pure core unsafe-free; any unavoidable native/OS boundary requires a narrow documented reviewed exception rather than blanket relaxation of repository rules.

title: Compatibility
requirement: Version wire semantics, evaluator, ABI, and database independently; do not silently change current v1 identities or add implicit legacy readers; preserve signed originals during explicit migration.

title: Verification
requirement: Every commit is tested, self-reviewed, independently reviewable, and known-good relative to an explicit baseline; maintain schema parity, formatting, linting, docs, security, fuzz, and package gates.

title: Operational rollout
requirement: Shadow release gating first, independent review, then explicit enforcement; rollback to known-good evaluator or pause promotion, never permissive fallback.

title: Ownership
requirement: Assign semantic, trust, execution, storage, platform, and release owners; document supported-host capabilities, incident response, and dependency governance.

title: Spec-first workflow
requirement: Durable approved specs anchor incremental code changes; follow ordered commits and preserve unrelated work; record deviations and unresolved decisions rather than inventing product rules.

title: No premature readiness
requirement: The approved design and this package are not implemented functionality, successful tests, or certification; report verification honestly and keep release authority disabled until gates pass.

title: Policy/profile selection
requirement: Select exact policy/profile revisions with explicit known values and duplicate rejection; protected modes cannot fall back to development defaults.

title: Structured inspections
requirement: Structural checks and trusted inventory establish actual artifact roles/exposure; incomplete or untrusted inventory cannot prove absence.

title: Acquisition versus conformance
requirement: A successful runner exit or completed selection is not conformance; empty accidental selections fail visibly and policy minimums govern evaluation.

title: Repo governance
requirement: Preserve useful xtask constraints while admitting approved spec/docs and necessary platform work; use native Rust automation, exact pins, and no generated state or credentials in Git.

title: Agent output contract
requirement: After each step report files, commands/results, review, commit SHA, baseline exceptions, risks, and whether the next step is safe; do not silently skip/merge/reorder/broaden steps.

title: Deployment verification
requirement: Authorization binds exact artifacts, destination/channel, policy, deviations and validity; deployment checks it, and transformed artifacts need explicit provenance or reevaluation.

title: Transport versus trust
requirement: Schema parsing, storage lookup, local process privilege, and imported signatures are distinct boundaries; payload claims never become trusted capabilities.
